content.comment_body: Hello, If the [product_name] main module is powered with 230 VAC and you have a 230 V expansion module (relay), can you also add 24 V expansion modules such as [product_name] in the last available slot? Can the inputs of the [product_name] analog expansion module tolerate 24 VDC, even when programmed as 0-10 V inputs? Is this behavior similar to the universal inputs found on the 12/24 VDC main module? [user_name] Translated with [company_name] ([product_name])

[company_name] manuals do not provide specific details about this scenario. Based on experience, the behavior should be consistent with base modules that have 0-10 V inputs. For a definitive answer, it's best to contact [company_name] support directly through their official channels.

If an analog expansion module is installed after the last 230 VAC module, it is possible to add 12/24 VDC digital expansion modules further to the right, but not additional 230 VAC modules. The reason is that analog expansion modules are electrically isolated on the bus and input side.
I recommend following the instructions in the official device manual rather than experimenting with the setup. Regards, [user_name] (translated with Google)
The user never stated an intention to experiment. What makes you think this?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing how to safely connect analog and digital expansion modules with varying voltage specifications to a 230 VAC-powered [product_name] main module. There is uncertainty due to incomplete or unclear documentation from [company_name] regarding sequencing and electrical isolation. Users are relying on personal experience and caution and emphasize the need for official clarification.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to understand if it is safe and permissible to combine 230 VAC and 24 V expansion modules with a [product_name] main module. Clear and dependable information about connection rules and input tolerances is expected.
